text:
megan: heads up — we saw a big spike in Pending pods in gpu-prod us-west-2 around 09:12, Karpenter started ~35 GPU nodes in parallel and we hit IP/eni limits + some cold-start failures :grimacing:
raj: ugh, classic thundering-launch. did we hit ENI exhaustion or some AWS quota?
oliver: ENI + ip-per-node. Cloudwatch shows ENI throttle errors and several nodes never registered because kubelet timed out during bootstrap.
sophia: probably two issues: (1) provisioner allowed explosive launches, (2) kubelet bootstrap/volume mounts were slow for that instance type.
megan: logs: infra-bot reported these from the provisioner controller: `RateLimitExceeded: Request limit exceeded for CreateNetworkInterface` and Karpenter events showed lots of "provisioning" -> "failed" transitions.
dinesh: we also saw a bunch of driver-install timeouts on the GPU AMI — NGC driver install sometimes blocks node readiness for 6-8m. combined with simultaneous launches that's bad.
raj: short-term mitigation: lower maxProvisioned in the provisioner or add a launch-rate limiter. can we gate new node launches with a token bucket?
sophia: Karpenter doesn't have a native token-bucket but we can add a simple workaround: split into multiple provisioners with different priorities/taints and use PodTopologySpread or scheduling constraints to prefer warm pool.
oliver: another option: pre-warm a small warm pool (2-4 nodes per AZ) with GPUs and set ttlSecondsAfterEmpty to keep them around. That avoids cold-start driver installs.
megan: proposed immediate actions: 1) reduce provisioner limits to 10 concurrent nodes, 2) enable warm pool, 3) add jitter/backoff on provisioner webhooks. anyone object?
dinesh: +1 on warm pool. also we should make the driver install non-blocking: move driver install to daemonset that tolerates NotReady and mark node Ready only after driver? but kubelet readiness gating still matters.
raj: for ENI/IP we should also adjust subnet sizing and check ENI trunking: enable IP trunking where possible and ensure CNI is configured for higher ip-per-node on burst nodes.
sophia: adding a small YAML snippet that folks can try; it reduces the provisioning burst and prefers cheaper fallback instance types:

```
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-throttle
spec:
  limits:
    resources:
      cpu: 1000
      memory: 4000Gi
  ttlSecondsAfterEmpty: 300
  provider:
    subnetSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: us-west-2
    securityGroupSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: default
  consolidation: true
  requirements:
    - key: kubernetes.io/arch
      operator: In
      values: [amd64]
    - key: karpenter.sh/instance-category
      operator: In
      values: [gpu,stable]
  limitsPerZone: 10
```

oliver: nice. Also consider adding `taints` on warm pool nodes like `prewarmed=true:NoSchedule` and use a PodSpec `tolerations` in a small subset or have a webhook that migrates pods to warm pool for cold-start sensitive jobs.
megan: longer-term: evaluate adding a launch-rate controller in front of Karpenter that enforces a global rate and per-AZ caps. Might be simpler than juggling many provisioners.
raj: agree. Also add tests in chaos env: simulate 200 pods scheduled to GPUs and assert we don't exceed ENI quotas or OOM kubelet.
dinesh: question about consolidation: when consolidation is on, nodes can be removed aggressively and cause more churn. maybe relax consolidation window so we don't churn when warm pool is doing its job.
sophia: good call. set `consolidation: manual` during peak windows or ramp consolidation TTL.
megan: action items I captured: 1) apply temporary provisioner limits (megan), 2) spin up 6-node warm pool across AZs (oliver), 3) check ENI/trunking settings and subnet CIDR (raj), 4) bake a faster AMI with preinstalled drivers (dinesh), 5) run load test in staging to validate (sophia). I'll open a ticket and link the plan.
infra-bot: created issue INFRA-1892 "mitigate GPU provisioner burst / ENI exhaustion" assigned to megan, raj, oliver, dinesh, due 3 days. :white_check_mark:
megan: thanks — please react on the ticket with blockers. we'll monitor tonight's batch job window and revert if anything spikes. :thumbsup:
raj: one more note — add metrics for `karpenter.provisioner.launch_rate` and `node.driver.ready_duration` to Grafana so we can alert before quotas hit.
oliver: I'll add dashboards and an alert when ENI errors > 5/min.
sophia: and add a small doc snippet in ops playbook for "GPU cold start runbook". keep it short.
dinesh: otherwise +1. I think with warm pool + rate limit we avoid most of the thundering launch pain.
megan: closing the thread here. followups on the ticket.
